reason: Each test emulates a mobile viewport. WebDriver BiDi has no mobile viewport (Firefox), and stock WebKit's viewport emulation has no mobile flag and refuses `mobile: true` as Unsupported. The matrix row marks `isMobile` as present on every browser, which holds only for Chromium

Each test uses a device scale factor other than 1, and Strider takes that only with the mobile-viewport capability (`emulation.viewport.mobile`), which Firefox and stock WebKit lack, so the context is refused as Unsupported. SS-074, SS-076, and SS-093 also capture at CSS-pixel scale (`screenshot.cssScale`), which those browsers lack too (matrix option-page-screenshot-scale-value-css). The matrix row marks the device scale as present on every browser, which holds only for Chromium

A `toHaveScreenshot` golden comparison of a transformed element at device scale, against an image made with Playwright's browser builds and fonts, which Strider's pinned browsers don't match. The test checks nothing else

Relies on Playwright's internal `__testHookBeforeScreenshot` or `__testHookAfterScreenshot`, which throws or delays between a capture's preparation and the capture; Strider has no such hook. The viewport these tests check is the one Playwright's full-page and element captures resize, and Strider's captures don't resize it on Chromium (`cdpAdapter/capture.ts` captures beyond the viewport with a clip), so there is no restoration to test

Playwright's it.skip runs this only off Chromium (playwright#9757): Chromium never answers `Page.captureScreenshot` while the page's main resource is still loading, so there is nothing for any driver to capture. Strider's capture is dispatched and ends at its deadline as `Deadline.Timeout` (`dispatchedUnconfirmed`), which reports the missing reply as it is
